sites.ownership: The encoding chooser owns its one-shot response callback for the dialog lifetime.
sites.justification: Accept, cancel, and close signals must share one callback slot so the encoding response is delivered at most once while avoiding widget-owned callback cycles.

sites.ownership: The encoding chooser owns its close/response guard.
sites.justification: The closed handler intentionally owns the dialog state, while accept and cancel paths set this guard before closing so close cannot call the one-shot callback again.

sites.ownership: The compare controller owns its action-installed guard.
sites.justification: Compare is hidden from the main menu during active compare sessions by removing the window action, so a mutable guard tracks whether the action is currently installed.

sites.ownership: The compare dialog owns the mutable left-side source selection.
sites.justification: Button callbacks update the left compare source while keeping the dialog responsive without spreading selection state across window code.

sites.ownership: The compare dialog owns the mutable right-side source selection.
sites.justification: Button callbacks update the right compare source and keep the Compare button sensitivity in sync with the current selection.

sites.ownership: The paste-text dialog owns its close/accept guard.
sites.justification: The closed handler intentionally owns the dialog state, while the Compare button sets this guard before closing so the callback cannot receive both pasted text and cancellation.

sites.ownership: The paste-text dialog owns its optional response callback.
sites.justification: Accept and close signals share one callback slot so generated pasted-text compare requests are delivered at most once without strong widget callback cycles.
